cohort_construction.distinct: one generator seed per 48 patients (seed 20261103 + i, skipping seeds the generator cannot build), relabelled per cohort, up to 10,000 distinct patients
cohort_construction.replicated: beyond the distinct pool, copy k of pool patient j is `<id>~r<k>` with every time shifted by (1 + (37k mod 700)) whole days; no new variety
cohort_construction.streaming: the distinct pool is written to an ndjson file one seed at a time and read back a line at a time, replicated as it is read, into StoreBuilder.add
cohort_construction.queries: seeded random_query / random_windows from patterns/test_execution_store.py, anchored on the first cohort, identical for every size; windows follow the pool patient and its shift

limitations: One machine (see environment); no other hardware, operating system or storage was measured.
The data are synthetic. Event density, concept frequencies and sources reflect the generator, not a clinical record system.

Beyond the distinct pool the cohort is replicated: copies repeat the pool patients with a whole-day time shift and add no variety. Concept posting sizes, candidate sets and match outcomes therefore scale as exact multiples, which a real population would not.
Queries are 50 seeded random queries from the differential test's generator, not a clinical query mix.
Latencies are wall-clock times of one thread of Python and DuckDB with the thread setting stated; no tuning was attempted.
Above the profile size, the query phase runs fewer queries and repeats (see parameters), so its latency percentiles rest on fewer samples.
Peak memory is the process's maximum resident set size, which includes the interpreter and DuckDB buffers.
No exhaustive reference ran at scale; correctness at scale rests on the differential test at 48 patients and the optional check at 1,000.
